newsitem.title: USA: Vons tops Q3 forecasts, cancels call.
newsitem.headline: Vons tops Q3 forecasts, cancels call.

text.p: Supermarket chain Vons Cos Inc Thursday reported better-than-expected earnings and also cancelled a scheduled conference with analysts as it continued to study an unsolicited takeover bid by Safeway Inc.
"It's highly unusual to cancel their conference call. Basically, they haven't made up their minds yet," said one analyst.
Vons officials did not return calls, although a recorded message at its investor relations office stated that Thursday's conference call had been cancelled.

Vons, which Wednesday said it was studying Safeway's unsolicited $1.68 billion bid for stock it does not already own plus the assumption of about $600 million in debt, reported third quarter net rose to $29.4 million, or $0.66 a share, topping First Call's mean estimate of $0.57 a share.
"Vons blew away estimates," said Douglas Christopher, analyst with Crowell, Weedon, who was forecasting Vons to earn $0.50 a share, at the lower end of the range of estimates.
"Sales exceeded our estimates by $20 million, gross profit margins were up and Vons managed to cut administrative expenses more than expected," Christopher said.
Christopher said Safeway's bid, which values Vons at about $56.28 a share based on Safeway's closing price Wednesday, would be good for Vons shareholders.
But, he added, "I think on a standalone basis, Vons is a very solid company. With the momentum they have and with their strong and consistent sales, a higher bid shouldn't be ruled out," he said.
On Wednesday, a group of Vons shareholders filed suit to block the proposed takeover on ground the bid was unfair. Safeway had no immediate comment on the suit.

Many analysts believe that the proposed deal between Safeway, which already owns 34.5 percent of Vons, was generous and will be completed, particularly since investment firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co, which owns 52 percent of Safeway, has thrown its support behind the deal.
KKR general partner Robert MacDonnell is a director of both Safeway and Vons, and KKR executive James Greene is a director of both.
"I don't know what Vons is thinking, but I know that KKR has always wanted to do friendly deals," Salomon Brothers analyst Jonathon Ziegler said.
